messages.subject: Examining replicate error help
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I have been going through the tutorial posted here: https://github.com/geomorphR/geomorph/wiki/Examining-replicate-error

I am trying to check my replication error of 35 samples with 13 landmarks, digitized twice.

I think I am in the minority here because I used CLIC -Coo to digitize my images and I have converted the .txt files to store them in .csv files. The .csv file used here is just id (id_rep#) and the landmarks (x1, y1, x2, y2,...)
I used the following code to create a matrix to do GPA:

tmp3<-as.matrix(read.csv("13 repeat field testing file2.csv",header=T, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
names3<-tmp3[,1]
tmp31 <- mapply(tmp3[,2:27], FUN=as.numeric)
tmp32 <- matrix(data=tmp31, ncol=26, nrow=70)
coords32<-arrayspecs(tmp32[,1:ncol(tmp32)],13,2)
dimnames(coords32)[[3]]<-names3
f13r<-gpagen(coords32)

I got the category information from another file:
field_cats<-read.csv("13 repeat field testing file.csv", header=TRUE)
cat_id<-field_cats$ID
cat_rep<-field_cats$Repeat
#Here the ID and Rep# are separated, so it would appear to have doubles ie (APR 011, APR 011....)

When I have run this:
procD.lm(f13r$coords ~ cat_id:cat_rep)

I get:
Call:
procD.lm(f1 = f13r$coords ~ cat_id:cat_rep)

Type I (Sequential) Sums of Squares and Cross-products
Randomized Residual Permutation Procedure Used
1000 Permutations

               Df       SS  MS Rsq  F Z Pr(>F)
cat_id:cat_rep 69 0.044885   0   1  0   0.5005
Residuals       0 0.000000 Inf
Total          69 0.044885

Where have I gone wrong?

Thanks,
Virginia

messages.body_plain:
Virginia,

There are a number of issues. The main one is that your specimen IDs are not the same for the first and second half:

APR 011 APR 019 APR 029 APR 040 APR 050 ARS 003 ARS 008 ARS 010 ARS 016 ARS 020 RMO 012

[12] RMO 020 RMO 024 RMO 029 RMO 037 RPV 009 RPV 018 RPV 025 RPV 037 RPV 045 SJU 001 SJU 004

[23] SJU 009 SJU 011 SJU 012 TLC 026 TLC 036 TLC 049 TLC 075 TLC 082 TPN 002 TPN 006 TPN 011

[34] TPN 016 TPN 018 APR011  APR019  APR029  APR040  APR050  ARS003  ARS008  ARS010  ARS016

[45] ARS020  RMO012  RMO020  RMO024  RMO029  RMO037  RPV009  RPV018  RPV025  RPV037  RPV045

[56] SJU001  SJU004  SJU009  SJU011  SJU012  TLC026  TLC036  TLC049  TLC075  TLC082  TPN002

[67] TPN006  TPN011  TPN016  TPN018

See ‘APR 011’ and ‘APR011’.  The space means these are treated as 2 objects, not the same object replicated. Thus, there are 70 objects in the dataset, not 35 with each repeated twice.

This may be solved, for your particular case, by generating a factor of the appropriate type, putting it in a geomorph data frame, and repeating:

id<-gl(2,35)

gdf<-geomorph.data.frame(coords=f13r$coords, id=id, rep=as.factor(cat_rep))

  procD.lm(coords~id:rep,data=gdf)

Virginia,

I used generate levels because your particular vector had the typos and I was not about to retype them properly (the space issue I mentioned). Normally one would just use their own vector and as.factor().

As for scaling, this depends on the question and the type of data. For landmarks, it is common to use aligned specimens after GPA so position and orientation are not considered. That means they are already scaled to centroid size = 1.0.

Dear Virginia,

as the author of the tutorial, let me offer some explanation of things that might help you.

procD.lm(Y.gpa$coords ~ ind:photo:rep)
# Y.gpa$coords is the 3D array of Procrustes residuals (shape data)
# ind is a vector containing labels for each individual
# photo is a vector designating whether the photo is 1 or 2
# rep is a vector designating whether the replicate is 1 or 2

Ind in this case should be a vector of labels for each individual, *without* replicate information. So if you have spec1, spec2, spec 3... Because you have replicates in there, there will be names written more than once.
Replicate then is a a vector of usually 1s and 2s (since many people do just 2 replicates), indicating if it is the first, second etc replicate of that specimen. Photo would also be like replicate.
Does this clarify things?
Emma

messages.body_plain:
Dear Chrissie,

You raise a very good question. So what is needed is that the new specimens are listed in the TPS for the digitize2d function to work properly. This is a functionality we can add to the next version, but for now, here is an easy fix:

filelist <- list.files() # use list.files to get a list of just the new pictures to digitise.
newdata <- array(0, c(nlandmarks, 2, length(filelist))) # change nlanmdarks to 47 for your data
dimnames(newdata)[[3]] <- as.list(filelist)
writeland.tps(newdata, "newTPSfile.tps") # write an empty tps file to the directory

Then open the new and your original tps files, and copy and paste the whole of the new onto the end of the old file. Then when all the pictures (old and new) are in the same working directory, with your newly appended tps file, digitize2d should work correctly.

Em

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] AIC with geomorph?
messages.body_plain:
Avi,

1. Yes, if you wish to do the math.  Because procD.lm or advanced.procD.lm objects provide residuals, you can calculate the error covariance matrix.  If you can get the error covariance matrix, you can calculate AIC.  The best way to calculate AIC for multivariate data, in my opinion, is presented by, Bedrick, E. J., & Tsai, C. L. (1994). Model selection for multivariate regression in small samples. Biometrics, 226-231.

Please note that we neither do nor will soon provide AIC or other information criterion values, nor implement an AIC model comparison function in geomorph, as the model selection theory for high-dimensional data (as GM data often are) is not well developed and is perhaps a bit contentious.  We do not wish to inadvertently suggest a theoretical leaning via implementation of tools that have not been well-tested.  I also have some personal concerns with AIC scores (and do not intend to speak for the rest of the geomorph team) with how weights are calculated (data dimensionality has strong influence), how delta-AIC scores should be valued, how practical parameter penalties are, and how small-sample corrections depend on sample size exceeding the number of variables.  I think there is a brighter future in evaluating model performance through MCMC approaches than using an index for ranking models.  But we have a ways to go to realize that future.

2. I’m not sure what you are asking here.  Is your question how to identify which effects are random, like the function lmer does?  Our functions do not have this capacity, as we only have functions that use least-squares or generalized least squares estimation of coefficients.  One can use nested.update to denote random effects for calculating F values in a limited capacity.

Best,
Mike

Chrissie,

Yes, there may be an issue for us to investigate here.

However, to get back to your original question (one of adding new specimens), a much simpler approach is to create a second tps file and digitize the new specimens with this.  Then, when you begin your study, simply read in 2 TPS files, append the specimens into a larger matrix, and go from there.

Because we are in R, there are myriad ways one can envision implementing this procedure (Note: I will ignore the obvious of ‘combine the files by hand in a text editor’, as such procedures are very prone to errors!). Below I list 3 R-based options:

1: Use the library ‘abind’ to combine data when reading in the files (the example is with NTS files, but the same could be used for TPS files):

https://github.com/geomorphR/geomorph/wiki/Reading-multiple-data-files

2: Read in the files and use ‘abind’ to combine them afterwards:

https://github.com/geomorphR/geomorph/wiki/Using-abind-to-Combine-3D-Arrays

3: Read in each datafile, convert them to matrices using ‘two.d.array’, use ‘rbind’ to combine them, and then ‘arrayspecs’ to create the 3D array of the combined datasets.

Hope this helps.

Dean

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] LM: outliers & switched (wrong order digitization)
messages.body_plain:
Avi,

We have included the outlier function in geomorph as a graphical diagnostic to aid users in identifying potential outliers. This function is particularly for helping to identify specimens which have been badly digitized, or where landmarks are digitized in the wrong order (a common data collection error).

However, we do not provide or even recommend a hard cut-off value for when specimens should be eliminated. Ultimately this is a user-decision, and making it an automatic component does not encourage user thinking about what outliers represent.  For instance, outliers may be incorrectly digitized specimens, they may be reflected specimens (another common occurrence) or they may be ‘good’ shapes that are extremely different relative to the rest of the sample.  Determining what they are and what to do with them is something the user must decide; not the software.

As for switching landmarks (ie, correcting landmarks which were digitized out of order), no we do not have a function for this.  The combinatoric possibilities of how users might incorrectly digitize their data is simply astronomical, and thus writing a function for correcting this sort of error is beyond most people’s programming capabilities (or at least, it is well beyond mine!).

messages.subject: geomorph updates
messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues,

I wish to alert you to a couple of geomorph updates, which are available with an installation of geomorph version 3.0.5, from Github (not yet available on CRAN).  These updates include:

- A new argument in advanced.procD.lm to choose among different distributions (SS, Rsq, or F) for estimating empirical effect sizes (Z-scores) and P-values
- An additional line of summary in ANOVA-producing functions (advanced.procD.lm, procD.lm, procD.pgls, and procD.allometry) to indicate from which distributions effect sizes and P-values were estimated
- Some small bug fixes and typo fixes

I also wish to alert you that a bug was pointed out in the previous version of geomorph (3.0.4) for calculation of sum of squares between models in the advanced.procD.lm function.  We have identified the error but have not fully identified the source and extent (whether under certain conditions or all conditions).  This error might have also been present in version 3.0.3.  Nonetheless, the updated coding in geomorph version 3.0.5 eliminated this error.  (We have tested the consistency in sums of squares, effect size, and P-value calculations across all functions that perform them, for various sum of squares types and effect sizes from various statistics.)  If you rely on ANOVA results from advanced.procD.lm from versions 3.0.3 or 3.0.4, you might want to rerun analyses with version 3.0.5 to confirm results.

Thank you to Avi Koplovich for brining this issue to our attention!

As a reminder, you can download geomorph directly from Github with the following single line of code:

devtools::install_gituhub(“geomorphR/geomorph”, ref = “Stable”)

Warm regards from Mike, and the geomorph team!
